title: Reinvent or Evolve? The AI Decision Most Enterprises Are Avoiding
summary: Most AI stalls at scale—because of operating models. Learn how to evolve or reengineer AI in customer experience delivery to unlock value
body_markdown:
By now, most organizations have successfully piloted a handful of AI use cases, whether it’s simple advisor assist or more complex workflow automation. Yet few have translated those early wins into end-to-end execution across the customer journey. And as customer expectations for speed, personalization, and seamless engagement continue to rise, those outdated operating models are showing their limits.


Despite all the hype (and hope), AI isn’t replacing services overnight.


## Why Most AI Programs Stall at Scale


Enterprise environments are complex, fragmented, and constrained by legacy systems, inconsistent knowledge bases, and regulatory requirements. How work gets done is often the biggest obstacle to scaling those AI pilots into production.


AI is often deployed as a layer on top of existing processes, rather than embedded into how journeys are designed and executed. That’s why organizations see pockets of improvement, but struggle to drive consistent outcomes at scale.


It’s also where (and why) the conversation needs to change.


As AI adoption matures, enterprises are approaching a more fundamental decision: *Should they evolve their existing operating model, or reengineer it entirely around AI?*


This isn’t a question of “more AI” versus “less AI.” It’s a choice between two fundamentally different approaches to delivering AI in customer experience. One model enhances human-led service with AI-driven support. It’s built around improving productivity, quality, and consistency. The other shifts AI into a leading role, with human teams focusing on complex cases and high-value interactions.


Most organizations won’t adopt one path universally. Instead, they’ll need to apply both approaches strategically across different journeys depending on complexity, risk, and operational maturity.


## Why Does This Matter Now?


The economics of service delivery are already shifting. Traditional, labor-led models—especially those built around repetitive, high-volume tasks—are becoming less sustainable, while new value is emerging around orchestration, insight, governance, and outcome-driven execution.


Organizations that fail to align their operating model with this shift risk higher costs, fragmented experiences, and slower adaptation to market demands.


At the same time, many enterprises remain stuck in that pilot mode, testing isolated AI use cases without redesigning the broader system those use cases depend on. The result is a widening gap between companies that operationalize AI and those that never move beyond experimentation.


The question enterprises are increasingly facing is how to redesign their operating models to make AI work: at scale, across the entire customer journey.
